overview.headline: Binary search halves a sorted array interval to find a key

keyPoints.point: Students learn that binary search repeatedly divides a sorted array interval in half to locate a key.
keyPoints.quote: Search a sorted array by repeatedly dividing the search interval in half.

keyPoints.point: Students learn to narrow the interval to the lower half when the search key is less than the middle item.
keyPoints.quote: If the value of the search key is less than the item in the middle of the interval, narrow the interval to the lower half.

keyPoints.point: Students learn to repeatedly check until the value is found or the interval is empty.
keyPoints.quote: Repeatedly check until the value is found or the interval is empty.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that binary search may be effective with an ordered linked list despite traversal costs.
keyPoints.quote: Binary search may be effective with an ordered linked list.
